about: Gates end the conversation; criteria are trade-offs. A hard gate puts a deal out. A soft gate keeps it visible but flags it, takes a Fit penalty, and asks you to write down why you're still looking. 'digest-only' gates are applied by the listing digest when it screens alerts, but have no checkbox in the Scorecard. 'builtin' gates are calculated from the deal's numbers; the rest are checkboxes you tick per deal. Every template can be switched off, retiered or reworded, and you can write your own.

builtin.label: Total project over your cap
builtin.explain: Total project = (asking price + inventory sold on top) x your project factor. Over your cap, the deal is out.
builtin.digestRule: Skip when (asking + inventory sold on top + any real estate sold separately) x project factor is over the cap.

builtin.label: Declining revenue
builtin.explain: Trips when the figures shown are down. Overrulable later (once revenue is confirmed and the cause understood), which turns it into a soft gate.
builtin.brokerQ: Why is revenue declining, and what does year-to-date look like?
builtin.digestRule: Skip only when figures the listing actually shows are falling. Never infer a decline from wording; no trend data is not a decline.

builtin.label: SDE under your floor
builtin.explain: Seller's discretionary earnings below the minimum you set in Money.
builtin.brokerQ: Any add-backs missing from the SDE figure? How flexible is the price given the earnings?

builtin.label: Fails the loan-coverage test at asking price
builtin.explain: DSCR (money left to pay the loan after your salary, divided by loan payments) below your coverage floor. Soft, because price is negotiable.
builtin.brokerQ: Is the asking price firm? Would the seller carry part of it as a note?

builtin.label: Cash-only, and it costs more than your cash
builtin.explain: The seller won't take bank financing and the total project is more than your cash down.
builtin.brokerQ: Would the seller accept an SBA buyer or carry a note, or come down on price?

builtin.label: Past your commute limit
builtin.explain: One-way drive longer than your limit for how often you'd need to be there.
builtin.brokerQ: How often does the owner actually need to be on site?

builtin.label: Land lease
builtin.explain: The business owns the building but leases the ground under it.
builtin.brokerQ: Land lease terms: years remaining, rent escalations, renewal rights?

builtin.label: Turnaround with a non-operational problem
builtin.explain: The business is in trouble for reasons operations can't fix: a dying market, legal or regulatory trouble, a lost anchor contract.
builtin.brokerQ: What's driving the problem, and what has the owner already tried?

templates.label: Food service
templates.explain: Any business that needs licensing for fresh or unpackaged food. A shop selling only packaged goods passes.
templates.digestRule: Restaurants, cafes, bakeries, food trucks, caterers, and shops with a deli or hot-food counter.

templates.label: The owner role needs hands-on trade knowledge
templates.explain: Test: would you need to know the trade to run it? A trade business with its technicians in place, where the gap is operations, passes.
templates.digestRule: Gate only when the owner must personally hold or perform the licensed trade work.

templates.label: Outside my region
templates.explain: Outside the area you set in Geography (a state, a metro, a country). A remote business you can run from home passes.
templates.digestRule: Gate only when the operation physically sits outside the region and needs presence there.

templates.label: The owner is the product
templates.explain: Nothing transferable: a personal brand, an artist's own work, a solo practitioner's practice with no other providers.
templates.digestRule: Solo practitioner or personal-brand businesses with no other providers.

templates.label: Operations outside my country
templates.explain: For online businesses: where the operations are, not just where the company is registered. US SBA loans generally need a US business ⚑ verify.
templates.digestRule: Skip online businesses whose operations are abroad. If the listing doesn't say, load it with a flag.

templates.label: Route businesses
templates.explain: Distributor, delivery, vending or service routes sold as a fixed circuit of stops.
templates.digestRule: The title or description calls it a route, or what's being bought is a fixed circuit of stops worked by a driver. A multi-crew service company that schedules in routes loads with a flag.

templates.label: Fintech
templates.explain: Businesses whose product is moving, lending, holding or trading money. Money-adjacent services (tax prep, bookkeeping, insurance agencies) pass.
templates.digestRule: Payment processing, merchant services, lending, crypto or trading tools, money transmitters, check cashing.

templates.label: Franchise resale
templates.explain: You'd be buying into a franchisor's rules, fees and approval process.
templates.brokerQ: Franchise fees and royalties, years left on the agreement, and the franchisor's transfer requirements?
templates.digestRule: Listings described as a franchise resale. Franchise ads in alert emails are not listings.

templates.label: Licensed health care
templates.explain: Clinics and practices that need licensed providers and insurance billing.
templates.digestRule: Medical, dental, therapy or pharmacy businesses that bill insurance or need licensed providers.

templates.label: Industries I won't own
templates.explain: A list you write: industries you won't put your name on, whatever the numbers say.
templates.digestRule: Skip listings in the industries named in this gate's text.

templates.label: Online-only businesses
templates.explain: If you only want a place you can walk into.
templates.digestRule: SaaS, apps, content sites, e-commerce with no physical operation.

templates.label: Home-based (nothing physical to buy)
templates.explain: Run from the seller's house, often a sign the owner is the business.
templates.brokerQ: What exactly transfers: customer list, contracts, equipment, staff?

custom.label: Your words
custom.explain: One sentence: what trips it, and what passes.
custom.brokerQ: For soft gates: the question that would clear it.
custom.digestRule: Optional: how the digest should recognize it in a listing.
